NOT a scriptural quotation but the common noun נבל (harp/lyre), so the MT check of step 5 is replaced by Migne's own three-language gloss in the same clause: nebel / ψαλτήριον / organum. Migne's type here shows no vowel points at this copy's resolution and none are supplied — the consonants are read, the pointing is not asserted. ⚑ The parentheses AND the trailing comma sit INSIDE the <foreign> element, which looks odd but is the source's own convention: CC encodes the Greek in this very clause as '<foreign xml:lang="greek">ψαλτήριον,</foreign>', comma included. The reason is mechanical — the chunker strips an unrecognized tag by replacing it with whitespace, so anything left outside comes through as '( נבל ) ,' with spaces Migne does not print, and a stray space before a comma is the very scar this patch exists to remove. (1) `locutus egomet` -> `locutos`: at 900 dpi the glyph is ambiguous, and `locutus` (perfect deponent, 'and afterwards I myself spoke') is correct Latin where `locutos` is a solecism -- a patch needs positive evidence, and applying this would have corrupted good Latin into an error. A damaged `p` that images as `r` is the condition of THIS COPY's inking, not a reading of the edition; restoring it would import a defect that exists nowhere but in one physical leaf. Compositor errors (wrong sorts SET) are restored; ink damage is not. That line is new and is the reason `iniquitetem` and `Nocere` ARE restored while `rossit` is not. (3) `Desiderabilia` -> `Desiderabillia` deferred: two occurrences stand in col 0871D and the report does not say which, so the leaf must be re-read rather than guessed.
